translationRepairs: In the fourth year (569), Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, who fled to the enemy and yielded the city to them.
In the fourth year (569), Northern Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, and the city went over to them.

盜殺 records that Kongcheng garrison commander 能奔達 was killed; 以城應之 then says the city went over. The original relative clause makes the slain commander also flee and surrender the city by misreading 奔達 as verbs.
Year 4, Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, who fled and reached them, yielding the city to them.
Year 4, Qi general Dugu Yongye came to raid; bandits killed Kongcheng garrison commander Neng Benda, and the city went over to them.
The same clause 盜殺孔城防主能奔達 names the commander 能奔達; 奔達 is not ‘flee and reach.’ 以城應之 is the city’s going over after his death.
Northern Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kangde, when Yuwen Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
Northern Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kang, learning that Yuwen Xian's troops had arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
The person is 新蔡王王康; 得以憲兵至 is the circumstance that Xian’s troops had arrived, not a given name Kangde. The replacement restores the name and keeps the temporal clause.
Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kangde, when Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
Qi general Prince of Xincai Wang Kang, when Xian's army arrived, quietly withdrew his force by night.
Literal English likewise fuses 得以 into Wang Kangde. 王康 is the name and 以憲兵至 marks when Xian’s army arrived.
Yuwen Xian had Pillar-of-State Tan Gonghui build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
Yuwen Xian had Pillar-of-State Hui, Duke of Tan, build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
柱國、譚公會 is office, ducal title 譚公, and given name 會, not a personal name Tan Gonghui. The repaired English matches that analysis.
Xian had Pillar-of-State Tan Gonghui build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
Xian had Pillar-of-State Hui, Duke of Tan, build Shidian city as relief for Fen Province.
The same punctuation 柱國、譚公會 separates rank from 譚公 plus 會; literal Tan Gonghui is a false fused name.
When High Ancestor reached the capital, Xian with Prince of Zhao Zhao both entered to bow in thanks.
When High Ancestor reached the capital, Xian with Zhao, Prince of Zhao, both entered to bow in thanks.
趙王招 is Zhao, Prince of Zhao. ‘Prince of Zhao Zhao’ stacks title and given name as if a doubled personal name; the repaired order matches the idiomatic line and the Chinese title-plus-name.
Moreover as the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, he always treated him with friendship and respect.
Moreover, because Zhi was the emperor's younger brother by the same mother, Xian always treated him with friendship and respect.
After 直內深忌憲，憲隱而容之, 帝之母弟 is Zhi (cf. 太后之子), and 每加友敬 is Xian’s treatment of him. Bare he/him can reverse the uterine-brother relation, which s0091’s 異生 contradicts for Xian.
You are the empress dowager's son by partial favor and specially cherished.
You are the empress dowager's own son and have received her loving care in special measure.
汝親太后之子 is ‘you are the dowager’s own son,’ not ‘son by partial favor.’ 偏荷慈愛 means he especially received her loving care.

At the time Pillar-of-State Prince of Chen Chun halted the army at Thousand-Li Path; Grand General Yongchang Gong Chun encamped at Roosting-Chicken Plain; Grand General Yuwen Sheng held Fen River Pass—all under Xian's command.

At the time Pillar-of-State Chun, Prince of Chen, halted the army at Thousand-Li Path; Grand General Chun, Duke of Yongchang, encamped at Roosting-Chicken Plain; Grand General Yuwen Sheng held Fen River Pass—all under Xian's command.

陳王純 and 永昌公椿 are two officers both romanized Chun. Leaving 永昌公 as Gong and writing Prince of Chen Chun / Yongchang Gong Chun fails to translate the duke’s title and collides the two names; the repaired title order is accurate.
Yuwen Xian said: "I am only a great commander of Yu
Yuwen Xian said: "I am only the Yuhou Grand Commander
我虞 begins the office 虞候大都督, continued through the variant note and 候大都督耳. Yu is not a place; Yuhou Grand Commander is the office, and the split units then read as one title.
候大都督耳 continues 虞候大都督; Hou is not a personal name. After the office is restored on s0136, this unit correctly keeps only 耳 as ‘after all.’
Yuwen Xian then said: "I am the Son of Heaven's elder brother, Prince of Qi."
Yuwen Xian then said: "I am the Son of Heaven's younger brother, Prince of Qi."
太弟 is the emperor’s younger brother (taidi), not an elder brother. The replacement matches the kinship term.
Northern Qi forces besieged Jin Province day and night without cease.
The Northern Qi ruler besieged Jin Province day and night without cease.
齊主攻圍晉州 names the Qi ruler as the besieger, not generic Qi forces.
The next day he joined the great army at Jiezhou.
The next day he joined the great army at Jiexiu.
介休 is the place Jiexiu; Jiezhou misreads 休 as 州.
At the time the Northern Qi ruler had already fled to Ye; he left his cousin Prince of Ande Yan Zong to hold Bing Province.
At the time the Northern Qi ruler had already fled to Ye; he left his cousin Prince of Ande Yanzong to hold Bing Province.
延宗 is one given name, conventionally Yanzong. Spaced Yan Zong looks like surname Yan plus given Zong.
Northern Qi Prince of Rencheng Gao Ta, Prince of Guangning Xiao Heng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
Northern Qi Prince of Rencheng Gao Jie, Prince of Guangning Gao Xiaoheng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
任城王湝 is Gao Jie (湝 ≠ Ta); 廣甯王孝珩 is Gao Xiaoheng, not a split Xiao Heng. The repaired names match the Chinese.
Qi Prince of Rencheng Ta, Prince of Guangning Xiao Heng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
Qi Prince of Rencheng Jie, Prince of Guangning Xiaoheng, and others held and defended Xindu, with troops numbering tens of thousands.
Literal Ta and Xiao Heng likewise misread 湝 and 孝珩; Jie and Xiaoheng are the correct readings.
He also had the Northern Qi ruler write in his own hand to Gao Ta, saying: "The court has treated the latitude of the realm with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
He also had the Northern Qi ruler write in his own hand to Gao Jie, saying: "The court has treated Wei with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
手書與湝 addresses Jie, not Ta. 朝廷遇緯甚厚 uses the Qi ruler’s given name 緯 (Wei), not ‘latitude of the realm.’
He also had the Qi ruler write in his own hand to Ta, saying: "The court has treated the latitude of the realm with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
He also had the Qi ruler write in his own hand to Jie, saying: "The court has treated Wei with great kindness; the princes are unharmed.
The same 湝 and 緯 errors appear in the literal line; Jie and Wei restore the names.
Yuwen Xian reached Xindu; Gao Rui drew up battle lines south of the city, and Yuwen Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
Yuwen Xian reached Xindu; Gao Jie drew up battle lines south of the city, and Yuwen Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
湝陣於城南 is Gao Jie drawing up lines; Rui renders a different character and is not supported.
Xian reached Xindu; Rui drew up battle lines south of the city, and Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
Xian reached Xindu; Jie drew up battle lines south of the city, and Xian ascended Zhang Er's mound to observe them.
Literal Rui for 湝 is the same false reading; Jie is required.
Before long Wei Xiangyuan, the camp commander Gao Rui had appointed, feigned going out to reconnoiter the lines and thereupon surrendered with his troops.
Before long Yu Xiangyuan, the Leader of the Army Gao Jie had appointed, feigned going out to reconnoiter the lines and thereupon surrendered with his troops.
領軍尉相願 is Lingjun (Leader of the Army) Yu Xiangyuan, appointed by 湝 (Jie). Wei is the wrong reading of Xianbei 尉, and camp commander under-translates 領軍.
The next day they fought again; Yuwen Xian broke them, capturing and slaying thirty thousand men, and seized Gao Rui, Gao Xiaoyuan, and the others.
The next day they fought again; Yuwen Xian broke them, capturing and slaying thirty thousand men, and seized Gao Jie, Gao Xiaoheng, and the others.
擒湝及孝珩等 captures Jie and Xiaoheng. Rui and Xiaoyuan do not match 湝 or 孝珩.

The emperor thereupon sent Junior Tomb Director Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Yuwen Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"

The emperor thereupon sent Junior Grand Steward Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Yuwen Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
小冢宰 is the junior minister of state / grand steward (cf. earlier 治小冢宰), not a tomb office. Junior Tomb Director invents a funerary sense from 冢.

The emperor thereupon sent Junior Tomb Director Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"

The emperor thereupon sent Junior Grand Steward Yuwen Xiaobo to say to Xian: "The Three Excellencies' posts should belong to close kin and the worthy; now we wish to make Uncle Grand Preceptor, Ninth Uncle Grand Tutor, and Eleventh Uncle Grand Protector—what does Uncle think?"
The literal line repeats Junior Tomb Director for 小冢宰; Junior Grand Steward is the office.
They also killed Grand General of the Upper Army Wang Xing, Duke of Anyi, Upper Opener-of-Gates Dugu Xiong, and Opener-of-Gates Doulu Shao—all because they were intimate with Yuwen Xian.
They also killed Senior Grand General Wang Xing, Duke of Anyi, Upper Opener-of-Gates Dugu Xiong, and Opener-of-Gates Doulu Shao—all because they were intimate with Yuwen Xian.
上大將軍 is the senior grand-general rank, not command of an ‘Upper Army.’ The rest of the sentence is unchanged and accurate.
Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongao.
Cong, styled Qianli, was grand general and Duke of Zhongba.
中垻公 is Zhongba (垻). Zhongao misreads the phonetic of 垻.
